Chapter VI, Certain Objections, is the last chapter, and its third paragraph from the end reads word for word as the card: We also have our dream of a Garden: but it lies in a distant future. We dream that woman shall eat of the tree of knowledge together with man, and that side by side and hand close to hand, through ages of much toil and labour, they shall together raise about them an Eden nobler than any the Chaldean dreamed of; an Eden created by their own labour and made beautiful by their own fellowship. The colon, the semicolon, the capital G on Garden and the British spelling labour all match. The paragraph before it sets up the ancient Chaldean seer's Eden in the past, so the line stands on its own. Schreiner wrote in English, so there is no translation drift.
